# Founding Fuel: Business & Entrepreneurship — Batch 1 (March–May 2015)
## Dense Observations & Source Attribution

---

## ARGUMENTS FF MAKES REPEATEDLY

**People/talent as the central organizational challenge:**
- "Talent will be the single most important determinant of our success" — SOURCE: "Are people really your biggest asset?" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-03-16)
- FF critiques the bell curve: "enough management research to tell us that using a bell curve to grade the performance of people...is dangerously flawed" and notes GE and Microsoft "publicly admitted that the practice destroyed the sharing or collaborative culture inside the firm" — SOURCE: "Are people really your biggest asset?" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-03-16)
- "We still refer to people as resources, as if we had the option to 'exploit' them, like land or capital" — industrial-era thinking still dominant — SOURCE: "Are people really your biggest asset?" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-03-16)

**Purpose as organizational glue:**
- "I look upon purpose as the essential glue that will bind the organisation of tomorrow" — SOURCE: "The search for higher purpose" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-03-16)
- Apple's Tim Cook quoted: "not just making money. Making money might be a by-product, but it's not our North Star" — SOURCE: "Why chasing profit may be self defeating" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-06)
- The "Inside-Outside Way of Thinking": inner circle = why company exists (enrich lives), outermost = what company does — SOURCE: "Why chasing profit may be self defeating" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-06)

**Customer-centricity over product/profit obsession:**
- "Thinking from the customers' point of view creates winners" — SOURCE: "Thinking from the customers' point of view creates winners" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-07)
- Apple Retail "was set up not to sell Apple products, but to establish and deepen the relationship between the company and its customer" — SOURCE: "The new mantra of consultative selling" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-26)
- Amazon's "anticipatory shopping" and predictive algorithms as highest expression of proactive customer service — SOURCE: "What successful companies do to win customer loyalty" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-04)

**Disruption as structural imperative for Indian firms:**
- "Indian businesses are skipping an entire generation of evolution" — SOURCE: "How to Build Your Business 2.0" by Haresh Chawla (2015-04-06)
- Three modes of startup attack: Disruption, Dissection, Diversion — SOURCE: "How to Build Your Business 2.0" by Haresh Chawla (2015-04-06)
- "Unless your business is protected by regulation, licences, strong intellectual property (IP) or a brand, beware, there is a startup somewhere waiting to eat your lunch" — SOURCE: "How to Build Your Business 2.0" by Haresh Chawla (2015-04-06)

**Entrepreneurial mindset inside corporations:**
- "Every company and board wants an 'entrepreneurial' leader" — the "professional entrepreneur" as ideal type — SOURCE: "Who wants to be CEO?" by Haresh Chawla (2015-03-26)
- ICICI, Mahindra, Tata cited as Indian corporations that successfully "unleashed entrepreneurial energy" — SOURCE: "Who wants to be CEO?" by Haresh Chawla (2015-03-26)

**Trust as foundational for founding teams:**
- "Most start-ups, the world over, fold up within the first year of their coming into being. And most of them do so not for external reasons but because their founders part ways" — SOURCE: "Trust is built at Ground Zero" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-27)
- The "flag-move-revisit-resolve approach as against a don't-ask-don't-tell approach" — SOURCE: "Trust is built at Ground Zero" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-27)
- Written roles and responsibilities for founders, not just employees: "pretend that you are big" — SOURCE: "Why disagreements between co-founders are good" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-11)

**Business model innovation over product/strategy innovation:**
- "In the future though, success will be determined not as much by strategy, but by how innovative a business model is" — SOURCE: "How to build a business model" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-24)
- Monitor Group study: most successful innovations "focus on shifts in the business model and customer experience" and "employ multiple kinds of innovation—frequently six or more" — SOURCE: "How to build a business model" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-24)

**Frugality and execution over funding as markers of real entrepreneurship:**
- "Did Dhirubhai Ambani go to IIT? Did somebody found Infosys with experience in a strategy firm?" — SOURCE: "An ecosystem of style over substance?" by Navroz Mahudawala (2015-03-30)
- "Innovation (or jugaad) comes with frugality - not with a few million dollars in your bank account" — SOURCE: "An ecosystem of style over substance?" by Navroz Mahudawala (2015-03-30)

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India's regulatory/structural problem is unique:**
- India's regulatory framework described as based on a "jail principle; intended to stop criminality, not encourage enterprise" — SOURCE: "Breaking the stalemate" by Dinesh Narayanan (2015-03-22)
- "India doesn't have an entrepreneur-friendly culture. Regulations are overwhelming. The government's answer to people breaking the laws is writing more laws, not enforcing them" — SOURCE: "Don't comment on the library. Read the books" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-19)
- India ranks "142 out of 189 countries on the ease of doing business" — SOURCE: "Either you share or you lose" by Haresh Chawla (2015-05-11)
- "The closed nature of the economy bred oligopolistic tendencies and established powerful linkages between a few industrialists, administrators and lawmakers" — SOURCE: "Breaking the stalemate" by Dinesh Narayanan (2015-03-22)

**India's talent management problem is specific to entrepreneurial firms, not large corporations:**
- "Most of what we know about talent management is based on our understanding of big corporations...if our entrepreneur went back to business school today, it is unlikely that he'd emerge any wiser than he already is" — SOURCE: "Are people really your biggest asset?" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-03-16)

**Indian MBA needs to be fundamentally different:**
- "India's biggest management challenges lie in execution and getting things done in a complex environment" — needs focus on implementation, not decision-making — SOURCE: "How to create an Indian MBA" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-26)
- Indian MBAs must "manage government and other stakeholders" and get things done "without structures and processes that dominate large Western companies" — SOURCE: "How to create an Indian MBA" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-26)
- Only 3 Indian B-schools AACSB accredited despite India accounting for "a quarter of all global business schools" — SOURCE: "How to create an Indian MBA" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-26)

**India's startup ecosystem is importing dysfunction along with energy:**
- "We are importing the hoopla - along with what some would call crazy valuations - from beyond our shores!" — SOURCE: "Rejoice, 'tis the season of high valuations!" by Sachin Joneja (2015-03-30)
- The ecosystem demands IIT/IIM pedigree, McKinsey/BCG experience, willingness to show Rs 5,000 crore scale in 5 years — but this excludes legitimate entrepreneurs — SOURCE: "An ecosystem of style over substance?" by Navroz Mahudawala (2015-03-30)

**India's infrastructure deficit makes the sharing economy more powerful here than in the West:**
- "India has massive unutilized captive infrastructure—historically poor physical infrastructure and lack of reliable third-party services providers compelled firms to create infrastructure" — SOURCE: "Either you share or you lose" by Haresh Chawla (2015-05-11)
- Setting up a salon requires "25-odd licences and municipal permissions" — SOURCE: "Either you share or you lose" by Haresh Chawla (2015-05-11)

**India's family business challenge:**
- "Since India has a large number of firms owned by business families, and family-based groups, Indian MBAs need the ability to get things done without structures and processes" — SOURCE: "How to create an Indian MBA" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-26)
- "The New Traditionals" — mid-sized family businesses like Alukkas and Chemmanur trying to professionalize without losing heritage advantage — SOURCE: "The New Traditionals" by Harsh Vardhan (2015-03-26)
- The "love versus competence" 2x2 matrix applied directly to family business succession — SOURCE: "The love versus competence debate" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-17)

**India's safety record as symptom of misaligned incentives:**
- "India has the worst safety record in the world, with as many as 1.4 million serious road accidents every year" — chairman of India's leading carmaker unwilling to raise safety standards without regulatory compulsion — SOURCE: "The tech route to safety" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-03-16)

**Jignesh Shah as post-liberalization cautionary tale:**
- Shah as emblematic of the gap between entrepreneurial aspiration and the unreformed regulatory/political economy — "why did Shah not become the poster boy of post-liberalisation India?" — SOURCE: "Breaking the stalemate" by Dinesh Narayanan (2015-03-22)
- "since it became independent in 1947, India had believed in the mythological power of the state to deliver prosperity" — SOURCE: "Breaking the stalemate" by Dinesh Narayanan (2015-03-22)

**India cannot yet build global product companies:**
- Druva's Jaspreet Singh moved to Silicon Valley "because he thought he can't build a global product company from India" — SOURCE: "Don't comment on the library. Read the books" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-19)
- "You cannot name a global Internet product company from Japan or Germany. Those you can name—Facebook, Twitter, eBay, Google—are Silicon Valley-centric" — SOURCE: "Don't comment on the library. Read the books" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-19)

**Kolte-Patil as counter-example in real estate:**
- Rajesh Patil's refusal to use political patronage in real estate: "In 1989...I promised my parents that I would never associate myself with politicians" — SOURCE: "Rajesh Patil is building a different kind of real estate firm" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-05-04)
- IBM 11-year transformation project, Deloitte/KPMG governance, Ram Charan mentoring — peers called it "sacrilege" — SOURCE: "Rajesh Patil is building a different kind of real estate firm" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-05-04)

**Gallup data on Indian employee disengagement:**
- "in India, a mere 9 percent of employees are engaged, 60 percent are not engaged, and 31 percent are actively disengaged" — SOURCE: "Secrets of the highly-engaged employee" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-23)

**Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs** — applied to employee engagement; FF argues companies satisfy physiological needs but ignore safety, belonging, esteem — SOURCE: "Secrets of the highly-engaged employee" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-23); "Igniting the Spark in Your Employees" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-23)

**Business Model Canvas / Lean Canvas / Lean Startup** — Alexander Osterwalder, Ash Maurya, Eric Ries cited — SOURCE: "How to build a business model" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-24); "A time to reflect" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-29); "Lessons from a 4-day old start up" by Charles Assisi (2015-03-24)

**Love vs. Competence 2x2 Matrix** — original FF framework for family business succession and entrepreneurial choice — SOURCE: "The love versus competence debate" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-17)

**Hindu Trinity as organizational metaphor** — Brahma (founder/creator), Vishnu (CEO/sustainer), Shiva (creative destruction/reengineer) — SOURCE: "Having that sense of wonder" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-30)

**Network Effects as economic moat** — "As the number of users go up, the value of each user goes up. Uber, Twitter and Facebook have it. Usually, e-commerce companies don't" — SOURCE: "Don't comment on the library. Read the books" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-19)

**Growth Hacking** — Dropbox, Prezi, Evernote as canonical examples; "VP of growth is the new VP of marketing" — SOURCE: "Traditional marketing is dead" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-06)

**Gary Hamel's Management 2.0** — "the need to change the very building blocks or DNA of organizations" — SOURCE: "Adapt or Die" by CKGSB Knowledge (2015-03-30)

**Conscious Capitalism (Raj Sisodia)** — "just as a few human beings set great purposes for themselves and eventually achieve greatness, the best companies in the world have great purposes" — SOURCE: "The search for higher purpose" by Indrajit Gupta (2015-03-16)

**Behavioural economics (Fear of Regret, Conformity Bias, Social Proof)** — applied to Amazon's recommendation engine — SOURCE: "What successful companies do to win customer loyalty" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-04)

**Reciprocal and Likeability Principles** — applied to consultative selling model — SOURCE: "The new mantra of consultative selling" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-26)

**Pygmalion Effect** — "high expectations lead to better performance" — applied to co-founder trust building — SOURCE: "Why disagreements between co-founders are good" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-11)

**Oxytocin as trust hormone** — "When employees are trusted, a hormone called oxytocin gets released. This facilitates intimacy and social interaction" — SOURCE: "Secrets of the highly-engaged employee" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-23)

**Path Dependence** — explaining Infosys/TCS success and Jagdish Sheth's academic career — SOURCE: "What does it take to become a Management Guru?" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-04-06)

**Four Layers of Infrastructure** — physical, digital, intellectual, emotional — original framework attributed to Subroto Bagchi — SOURCE: "Building Your Company's Infrastructure" by Founding Fuel (2015-04-13)

**CK Prahalad** — referenced via Hamel collaboration ("core competence," "Competing for the Future") — SOURCE: "Adapt or Die" by CKGSB Knowledge (2015-03-30); also noted as Indian management academic who had to emigrate to achieve guru status — SOURCE: "What does it take to become a Management Guru?" by Rishikesha

# Founding Fuel Business & Entrepreneurship — Batch 2 (May–August 2015): Dense Observations

---

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES

**Age and entrepreneurship is a false constraint**
FF publishes three separate pieces challenging age-bias in entrepreneurship in the same week:
- "Are You Too Old to Be an Entrepreneur?" (Krishnan, May 13): "I don't see why age should be seen as a disqualification for entrepreneurship" — uses Aravind Eye Hospital's Dr. V, Shalini Urs of Myra, Steve Jobs at 52 (iPhone), and the author's own father at 42 as evidence.
- "Is Old the New Useless?" (FF, May 18): Directly rebuts Vinod Khosla's claim that "people above 45 basically die in terms of new ideas" as "dead wrong" and "misleading folklore" — marshals Ray Kroc (52), Colonel Sanders (65), Arianna Huffington (54), David Duffield (64 for Workday, 46 for PeopleSoft).
- Both pieces converge on Steve Jobs's *best* work (iMac, iPod, iPhone, iPad) coming after age 45.

**Capital efficiency over capital abundance**
- "How Not to Spend Your Capital" (FF, May 18): "Scarce capital forces you to think harder about your problems" — illustrates with Mindworks (US subsidiary overspend) vs. a bootstrapped niche IT company that solved costs by moving to Malaysia instead.
- "What About Those Who Don't Have War Chests?" (FF, July 24): CarToq.com achieved #2 auto media ranking with limited resources through focus, quality-over-quantity, and flexibility. "Customer money is always better than investor money" — SOURCE: "Building Enterprises That Last" (FF, July 25).
- "Cash Flow and the Three Other Measures" (FF, June 30): "For a start-up, it is all about cash flow. Every other financial parameter can wait."

**Disruption must be self-initiated**
- "Disrupt or Destroy Your Own Business" (FF, June 1): Amazon's Kindle (Lab126 skunkworks), Netflix's streaming pivot — both framed as proactive self-cannibalization. "You have to become your own fiercest competitor and disrupt or destroy your own business before competition does."
- "Why Digital Transformation Is So Difficult to Achieve" (FF, June 23): MindWorks's own experience — "Why postpone the inevitable?" They offered to automate a profitable project themselves, cutting their own billing by 40%.
- "You Are Only As Good As Your Next Big Idea" (FF, July 27): Rita Gunther McGrath's "transient competitive advantages" framework invoked — "the days of relying on a single sustainable competitive advantage are over."

**Strategy communication fails because of the "curse of knowledge"**
- "Why Don't Strategies Stick?" (FF, May 25): Kaplan and Norton statistic — only 5% of workforce understand company strategy. Elizabeth Newton's Stanford "tapper-listener" experiment used as the core explanatory mechanism. Solution: "clarity stories" / narrative.
- "Make Strategies Stick — Neutralize Stories That Undermine Them" (FF, July 7): Anti-stories are pre-existing organizational beliefs that defeat new strategies. "We can never fight an anti-story with a fact; we can only replace it with a better story."
- "Overturn Perceptions That Subvert a New Strategy" (FF, Aug 12): Three approaches that don't work — arguments, assertions, denial. Three that do — mea culpa, challenging generalizations with specific counter-stories, changing behavior.

**Design thinking and "unlearning" as entrepreneurial edge**
- "What Start-ups Ought to Do Now" (FF, May 25): "Designers train themselves to unlearn. They reimagine and rethink." Cites Aeron chair (Herman Miller), Chartcube's pivot from Excel-mobile to data-collaboration-cube. Acquisition spree by Google, Facebook, Adobe, McKinsey (via Fjord) of design firms cited as evidence of corporate validation.

**Growth hacking / behavioral science as systematic tools**
- "Develop a Growth Hacker's Mindset" (FF, May 13): Sean Ellis's 2010 coinage; Dropbox reward loop; Gmail invite scarcity; "Dead Space" advertising (iPhone signature). "Real people share experiences, the believability of the message is a jaw-dropping 70–92 percent compared with less than 45 percent when a brand owner makes similar claims."
- "How Zara, Sensodyne and Others Use Behavioural Science to Unlock Value" (FF, June 22): Loss aversion (Zara fast fashion), decoy pricing (The Economist), scarcity effect (OnePlus invite), expert bias (Sensodyne doctor). Framed as embedable business tools "at near zero cost."

**The Experience Economy as strategic imperative**
- "Why You Should Sell Your Brand as an Experience" (FF, June 17): Product Economy → Service Economy → Experience Economy progression. Starbucks assaulting all five senses as the canonical example.
- "A Brand Is Not Enough. Create a Cool Brand" (FF, July 30): BMW used to illustrate that cool brands deliver three things: promise, self-esteem boost, and identity projection. "Cool brands make us feel happy and good about ourselves."

**Employee-first as competitive strategy**
- "Why You Should Treat Your Employees as Well as Your Customers" (FF, July 1): Southwest Airlines (40 consecutive profitable years), Ritz-Carlton ("ladies and gentlemen serving ladies and gentlemen"), Starbucks (health insurance + stock options to entry-level "partners"). "Shift your focus from customers to your employees."
- "Transform Your Workplace Into a Fun Place" (FF, June 10): Google kindergarten-color office, "office collision" as idea-generation mechanism, laughter research from MIT/Wharton/London Business School. Role reversal thesis: "talent, the term companies use to refer to employees, is no longer working for the company; it is the company which is working for its talent."

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India's startup boom is geographically concentrated and may be overhyped**
- "Does India Mean Business?" (FF, Aug 15): 132,000 new companies in 21 months (Nov 2013–July 2015), ~6,200/month — "but a closer look reveals a stark divide between a few cities and the rest of India." Data from corporate affairs ministry used; heat map visualization of district-wise data.

**India's on-demand economy is structurally distinct from the West**
- "Making Money Off the Lazy Economy" (Haresh Chawla, June 8): "Someone told a bunch of enthusiastic startups this — that we Indians love to be serviced and pampered." ~30 on-demand@home startups; Chawla argues this will "probably become the largest tech-enabled assisted economy in the world." Smart-cab drivers earning Rs 80–90,000/month cited as evidence of wealth redistribution. "A country of cabs and courier boys!"
- The India angle is that low-cost labor + high service preference + smartphone penetration creates a unique structural opportunity not replicable elsewhere.

**India's innovation deficit is real, Valley-worship is the problem**
- "Indian Innovation: Too Much Valley Kool-Aid Without the Valley" (Baba Prasad, Aug 15): Directly engages Narayana Murthy's IISc speech — "Why has there been no earth-shaking invention or technology from India over the last 60 years?" Prasad argues the "flow of ideas is one-directional" — from West to India — and that Indian researchers absorb Western frameworks "as if they were divine truth." Calls for genuinely indigenous innovation thinking.
- Father-in-law narrative (Professor Nagarajan, Harvard PhD 1961, returned to build Poona University's English dept) used to illustrate "magic of the sixties" — idealistic return vs. today's brain drain/startup hype.

**Reliance as the test case for India's command-and-control corporate culture**
- "Why Reliance Is Struggling to Launch Its 4G Service" (FF, May 27): Rs 70,000 crore commitment; "crucial test for Reliance's top-down, centralised decision making model." Culture described: same project assigned to two separate teams without either knowing; public upbraiding at reviews; "revolving door for senior executives." Google-inspired wall colors described as "superficial at best." Yet: "the Reliance juggernaut has learnt to take all this in its stride."

**The Housing.com/Rahul Yadav episode as India-specific cautionary tale**
- "The Rahul Yadav Story You've Never Heard Before" (Haresh Chawla, July 3): Firsthand account — Chawla invested after meeting Yadav at Italian restaurant in Bandra. "His thinking was ten years ahead of the market." Describes the founder's evolution from "shy and quiet" to someone whose "confidence soar[ed]" destructively with funding. Framed explicitly as the misaligned VC-founder relationship in India's shallow ecosystem.
- "3 Reasons Why Every CEO Must Watch Dramatic Tragedy" (Baba Prasad, July 8): Uses Housing.com's "dramatic rise and the crash of its CEO Rahul Yadav" as the Indian entrepreneurial tragedy case.

**The Gig Economy's Indian dimension**
- "The Gig Economy" (Charles Assisi, June 8): India is the *largest* population on Fiverr (20% of all users vs. 16% US). Fiverr is the 176th most popular site for Indians. "itsmechetan" from Delhi holding sign at Jama Masjid for $5. Assisi notes absence of "any relevant Indian statistics" — the data gap itself is observed.

**Ujjivan as India-specific example of entrepreneurial excellence**
- "Cash Flow and the Three Other Measures" (FF, June 30): Ujjivan microfinance cited as "great example of building a consistent set of measures for employee perception" — founder Samit Ghosh doing employee surveys "from the time it was really tiny." Framed as counter-example to India's tendency to treat HR measurement as "warm and fuzzy."

---

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, MENTAL MODELS

**Repeatedly invoked:**
- **CK Prahalad's de-risking framework**: "Our job is not to take risks, our job is to de-risk the future" — crocodile moat/fortress metaphor — SOURCE: "The Difference Between Taking a Risk and Risky Behaviour" (FF, May 25)
- **Jim Collins** (Built to Last, Good to Great): Full interview — SOURCE: "Jim Collins on the Building Blocks of Greatness" (CKGSB Knowledge, June 15). Collins distinguishes "principles that last" from "companies that last."
- **Rita Gunther McGrath's transient competitive advantage**: SOURCE: "You Are Only As Good As Your Next Big Idea" (FF, July 27)
- **Steve Blank's Lean Startup**: Full interview; sea turtles as "physical VPNs" for Chinese startups — SOURCE: "Red Star Rising: A Q&A With Steve Blank" (CKGSB Knowledge, Aug 6)
- **Linda Hill's Collective Genius**: Full interview; demolishes "solo genius" myth; Pixar as evidence; millennial preference for co-creation — SOURCE: "Everybody Has a Slice of Genius" (CKGSB Knowledge, July 11)
- **JBS Haldane's "On Being the Right Size"** + Galileo's Square-Cube Law: Used to argue "everything has an appropriate size" — against bigness worship — SOURCE: "The Altar of Bigger" (FF, June 8)
- **Anders Ericsson's Deliberate Practice** (1993 paper): Invoked against "unconscious competence" as enemy of expertise — SOURCE: "Work Smart. Not Hard" (Kavi Arasu, Aug 18)
- **Behavioral science principles**: Loss aversion, scarcity effect, decoy pricing, expert bias, effort justification — SOURCE: "How Zara, Sensodyne and Others Use Behavioural Science" (FF, June 22); "How to Get Customers to Own Your Brand" (FF, May 20)
- **Sakichi Toyoda's 5 Whys**: SOURCE: "Why Questions Score Over Answers" (FF, June 26)
- **David Yoffie's (Harvard) question**: "What can you bet on, without betting the company?" — SOURCE: "The Difference Between Taking a Risk and Risky Behaviour" (FF, May 25)
- **Baba Prasad's Bear-and-Hikers vs. Broken Cup paradigms**: Simple agility (expedient, no long-term thinking) vs. strategic agility (handles failure as learning) — SOURCE: "Enabling Strategic Agility in Organizations" (FF, Aug 11)
- **Question Formulation Technique** (Dan Rothstein/Luz Santana, Right Question Institute): SOURCE: "Why Questions Score Over Answers" (FF, June 26)
- **HBR's four question types** (Clarifying, Adjoining, Funnelling, Elevating) — Pohlmann & Thomas — SOURCE: same article

---

## WHAT FF IS SKEPTICAL OF / PUSHES BACK AGAINST

**The age-youth fetish in VC investing**
- Investor comment to "Raj": "I was 27 when I started. You are probably too old for this thing" — treated as emblematic of a broken heuristic — SOURCE: "Are You Too Old to Be an Entrepreneur?" (Krishnan, May 13)
- Vinod Khosla's "people above 45 basically die in terms of new ideas" called "dead wrong" and propagating "a misleading folklore" — SOURCE: "Is Old the New Useless?" (FF, May 18)

**Raising capital as default/success metric**
- "A lot of start-ups mix up raising funds with success" — SOURCE: "Building Enterprises That Last" (FF, July 25)
- "Customer money is always better than investor money. It means you've got a value proposition" — SOURCE: same
- "Chasing that scale without a product-led differentiation will hurt you over time. A lot of the money getting burnt is actually evaporating" — SOURCE: same

**Asset-light/outsourcing dogma**
- "How to Reduce Cost and Gain Competitive Advantage" (FF, July 8): Dell outsourced to Asus until Asus outcompeted Dell. "Though Wall Street welcomes this move. It has even coined a seductive term for it: asset light." Wall Street framing explicitly critiqued.

**Milton Friedman's shareholder-primacy doctrine**
- "Conscious Capitalism" (FF, Aug 6): "Traditional companies believe that the business of business is to maximize profit for its shareholders to the exclusion of everything else. This school of thinking gained legitimacy following celebrated economist Milton Friedman's often-quoted article." Explicitly challenged via Triple Bottom Line / conscious capitalism framing.

**The "solo genius" mythology**
- Linda Hill interview: "demolishes the myth of the 'solo genius' who has an 'aha moment' leading to breakthrough innovation" — even Steve Jobs's Pixar is cited as evidence *against* the solo genius model — SOURCE: "Everybody Has a Slice of Genius" (CKGSB Knowledge, July 11)

**Bigness/scale worship**
- "The Altar of Bigger" (FF, June 8): "We seldom display this understanding [that everything has an appropriate size]. In our default mental position, a $10 million company is the same as another with $1 million in sales, only bigger and better." Ferran Adrià's El Bulli — "one exceptional restaurant yet make a seismic impact on the world" — as counter-icon.

**India's one-directional idea flow from the West**
- "Indian Innovation: Too Much Valley Kool-Aid Without the Valley" (Prasad, Aug 15): Ideas from West absorbed "as if they were divine truth" with no reciprocal flow. The headline itself is the critique.

**Command-and-control corporate cultures**
- "Why Reliance Is Struggling" (FF, May 27): "Employee engagement and empowerment, a company-wide culture of innovation and a high trust environment are the cornerstones of the modern day enterprise. Reliance's new ventures, on the other hand, have typically relied on a different and unique operating philosophy." Reliance culture described as a functional anomaly that somehow works — creating cognitive dissonance FF doesn't fully resolve.

# Founding Fuel: Business & Entrepreneurship — Batch 3 (Aug 2015 – Jan 2016)
## Dense Observations with Full Attribution

---

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES

### 1. The Online/Offline Inversion
FF consistently argues that the real value in India lies offline, not online, and that the dominant VC narrative around e-commerce is misallocated.

> "The pot of gold does not reside in a mobile app or a website. The potential to make real money lies offline." — SOURCE: "Never Mind Online. Come Offline" by Haresh Chawla (2015-08-20)

> "The funded-to-the-gills online retailers will hit a glass ceiling. They have blown-up (or invested if you want to be kind) money on deals and discounts to change consumer behaviour." — SOURCE: "Never Mind Online. Come Offline" by Haresh Chawla (2015-08-20)

Chawla cites a Kotak Institutional Equities report warning of the "Great Indian Online Myth" — only 40 million active e-commerce customers while $6 billion has been spent building this "small but not-so-loyal base." — SOURCE: "Never Mind Online. Come Offline" by Haresh Chawla (2015-08-20)

### 2. Startup Math Doesn't Add Up
